Hounslow's population increased by around 34,200 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 290,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Hounslow increased by 13.5%, from just under 254,000 in 2011 to around 288,200 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of London (7.7%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Hounslow was home to around 36.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 32.4 in 2011. This area was among the top 10% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Hounslow than across London

An older Hounslow

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Hounslow increased by three years, from 33 to 36 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than London as a whole in 2021 (35 years) but a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 35 to 49 years rose by just under 15,000 (an increase of 26.7%), while the number of residents between 25 and 34 years fell by around 6,000 (11.6% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 35 and 49 years increased by 2.6 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Marriage and civil partnership in Hounslow

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) increased in Hounslow, but fell across England.

In Hounslow, the percentage that said they were married (or in a civil partnership) rose from 46.0% in 2011 to 47.5% in 2021, while across England it fell from 46.8% to 44.7%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 40.2% to 40.0%.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Hounslow fell from 38.5% to 38.3%, while the percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 7.4%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Hounslow increased by 1.5 percentage points

Family in Hounslow

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased here, but fell across England.

In Hounslow, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 20.3% in 2011 to 22.1% in 2021, while across England it fell from 19.3% to 18.9%. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 17.8% to 18.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Hounslow fell from 13.3% to 12.2%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 6.5% to 7.1%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Hounslow increased by 1.8 percentage points

Employment in Hounslow

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell in this area, but rose across London.

In Hounslow, the percentage who were employed fell from 59.9% in 2011 to 58.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 58.6% to 59.4%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Hounslow increased from 4.4% to 4.5%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) decreased from 13.2% to 12.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Hounslow decreased by 1.1 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Hounslow (2.7 percentage points) than across England (0.6 percentage points).

In Hounslow, the percentage of adults in employment working 15 hours or less increased from 8.5% in 2011 to 11.3% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage across England increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Hounslow fell from 13.0% to 10.3%, while the percentage of adults in employment who worked 31 to 48 hours decreased from 61.8% to 60.7%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Hounslow increased by 2.7 percentage points

Hounslow residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 141,700 Hounslow residents said they were born in England. This represented 49.2% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 139,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 54.8% of Hounslow's population.

India was the next most represented, with around 38,000 Hounslow residents reporting this country of birth (13.2%). This figure was up from around 27,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 10.7% of the population of Hounslow.

The number of Hounslow residents born in Poland rose from around 10,400 in 2011 (4.1% of the local population) to around 11,100 in 2021 (3.9%).

In 2021, 49.2% of Hounslow residents reported their country of birth as England

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Hounslow (7.5 percentage points) than in nearby Richmond upon Thames (2.9 percentage points).

In Hounslow, the percentage of private renting increased from 23.4% in 2011 to 30.9% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Richmond upon Thames increased from 21.8% to 24.7%.

The rate of social renting in Hounslow fell from 22.8% to 21.0%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 50.1% to 45.7%.

Private renting in Hounslow increased by 7.5 percentage points

Disability in Hounslow

In 2021, 6.8% of Hounslow residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater in Hounslow (2.6 percentage points) than across London (2.3 percentage points, from 9.4% to 7.1%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Hounslow decreased by 2.6 percentage points

Unpaid care in Hounslow

In 2021, 3.5% of Hounslow residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 6.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.7% in 2011. The proportion of Hounslow residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 2.5% to 2.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Hounslow (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across London (2.6 percentage points, from 6.4% to 3.8%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Hounslow decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Hounslow

In 2021, 7.3% of Hounslow residents identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group"), up from 3.6% in 2011. The 3.7 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across London, the percentage of people from the "Other ethnic groups" ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 3.4% to 6.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 1.0% to 2.2%.

In 2021, 44.1% of people in Hounslow identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 51.4% in 2011), while 36.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 34.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 6.6% in 2011 to 7.2% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 7.3% of usual residents in Hounslow identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group")

Health in Hounslow

In 2021, 47.3% of Hounslow residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 42.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.7% to 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Hounslow residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 1.6% to 1.3%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.0% to 4.1%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Hounslow increased by 4.6 percentage points

Religion in Hounslow

In 2021, 18.6% of Hounslow residents reported having "No religion", up from 15.9% in 2011. The rise of 2.7 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Hounslow. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across London, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 21.0% to 27.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 38.3% of people in Hounslow described themselves as Christian (down from 42.0%), while 16.7% described themselves as Muslim (up from 14.0% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 18.6% of usual residents in Hounslow reported having "No religion"

National identity in Hounslow

Of Hounslow residents, 27.9% did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in 2021, up from 26.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 25 people (4.1%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 2.2% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Hounslow that identified as "British only" increased from 32.7% to 54.4%.

The percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was 22.5% (similar to 2011) across London. Across England, the percentage increased from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Hounslow increased by 1.9 percentage points
